source.title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus Toxic Shock Syndrome

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Only the target letter was atomized. Text from the preceding leishmaniasis letter and following SARS letter appears on the same PDF pages and was excluded.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors report a case of toxic shock syndrome caused by a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strain producing toxic shock syndrome toxin 1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report a case of TSS due to an MRSA strain that produced a TSS toxin 1 (TSST-1).

atoms.canonical_statement: The case patient was a 54-year-old woman admitted in Brussels after 2 days of myalgia, diarrhea, and vomiting, with palate surgery 2 months earlier and repeat surgery 2 weeks earlier.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 54-year-old woman was admitted to the emergency ward of Brugmann University Hospital, Brussels, with a 2-day history of myalgia, diarrhea, and vomiting. She had undergone surgery for a palate neoplasia 2 months earlier, and again 2 weeks earlier, in another hospital.

atoms.canonical_statement: Cultures of blood, stool, and urine were negative for microbial agents.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cultures of blood, stool, and urine samples were negative for microbial agents.

atoms.canonical_statement: Puncture of the operative wound released 12 mL of pus; pus culture yielded MRSA carrying the TSST-1 gene, which the authors detected by multiplex polymerase chain reaction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Puncture of the wound released 12 mL of pus; culture of the pus sample yielded an MRSA strain harboring a TSST-1 gene, detected by multiplex polymerase chain reaction as previously described (3).

atoms.canonical_statement: Molecular typing identified the isolate as MRSA pulsed-field gel electrophoresis clone G10 carrying SCCmec type II and belonging to the ST5-SCCmec II clone, formerly called the New-York/Japan clone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: By molecular typing, the strain belonged to the epidemic MRSA pulsed-field gel electrophoresis clone G10 and carried the staphylococcal chromosome cassette mec (SCCmec) type II. This clone belongs to the sequence type (ST) 5-SCCmec II clone, formerly named “New-York/Japan clone,”

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors cite a 2001 national survey reporting this epidemic clone in 12% of Belgian hospitals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This epidemic clone, which is widely disseminated in the United States, Japan, and Europe, has been found in 12% of Belgian hospitals during a national survey conducted in 2001 (6).

atoms.canonical_statement: The reported treatment included aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation, dopamine, 'teicoplamin' as printed on page 636, and clindamycin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The treatment included aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation, administration of dopamine, and antimicrobial agent therapy with teicoplamin and clindamycin.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that they immediately used teicoplanin and clindamycin because they suspected a nosocomial S. aureus infection, possibly MRSA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We immediately treated our patient with teicoplanin and clindamycin because we suspected a nosocomial infection with S. aureus, possibly MRSA.

atoms.canonical_statement: The clinical course was favorable: a diffuse macular rash appeared on day 2, acute renal failure and other laboratory abnormalities resolved, and extensive peeling of both hands developed by day 5.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The treatment outcome was favorable. On the second day, a diffuse cutaneous macular rash appeared. The acute renal failure and the biological abnormalities resolved. On the fifth day, the patient was transferred back to the hospital where she had undergone surgery; extensive peeling then developed on both of the patient’s hands.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors judged that the patient met toxic shock syndrome criteria and that bacteriologic findings confirmed staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our patient met the criteria of TSS: she had fever, rash, desquamation, hypotension, vomiting, diarrhea, myalgias, elevated creatine kinase, acute renal failure, and thrombocytopenia. The diagnosis of staphylococcal TSS was confirmed by bacteriologic results.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors describe this as the first European case of toxic shock syndrome due to TSST-1-producing MRSA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: this case is the first of TSS due to TSST-1–producing MRSA in Europe.

atoms.canonical_statement: The letter states that usual staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome recommendations at that time used a beta-lactamase-resistant antistaphylococcal agent and sometimes clindamycin to decrease TSST-1 synthesis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The usual recommendations for the treatment of staphylococcal TSS do not consider this possibility and consist of a β-lactamase–resistant anti-staphylococcal agent and clindamycin in some cases (to decrease the synthesis of TSST-1) (9–11).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that clinicians should consider MRSA when selecting initial antimicrobial therapy for toxic shock syndrome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The possibility of MRSA must be considered when initiating antimicrobial agents to treat TSS.
